top_choice_rationale: Anne Carson (P001) is my first choice on the common criteria. Her voice is cool, exact and recognizable, and it can turn suddenly to grief or desire. Autobiography of Red and Nox show formal invention tied to specific emotional and intellectual stakes. Her sustained engagement with Greek and Latin literature works as method, not decoration. Public knowledge of the essays (Eros the Bittersweet), the mixed lyric and prose volumes, The Beauty of the Husband and later books such as Red Doc> and Float suggests her method kept changing over decades, but I cannot confirm that these books reach the level of the two landmarks. The citation should credit only original written work in English (lyric, verse narrative, elegy and essay). Translations, adaptations and scholarship count as context for how the work arises, and book-object form is not credited. That scope answers the attribution objection. Her writing in English lets the committee judge her language directly, which reduces uncertainty but is not merit. The main risk is sustained quality beyond the landmark books, which should be tested against the mid-career and later volumes. I rank Cărtărescu (P002) second. His single long project has real strength, but I cannot judge from translation whether his recurring imagery is development or repetition. I rank no award (P000) last, because both proposals are substantive literary cases. My evidence rests on public knowledge and translations, not on independent verification or a full reading of either corpus.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile. The documented connections (Horace Engdahl, Daniel Birnbaum, the Kris circle, and the co-opted secretaries Mats Malm and Ingrid Carlberg) are not linked to any shortlisted writer. I disclose that I chair the committee and am one of the explicit P001 supporters. My own scholarly work on poetry, the fragment, exile literature and translation is context, not evidence of preference. Conflicts are disclosed and not adjudicated.
